To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
humanized Oatp1B1 and Oatp1b3 mice have moderate compensatory changes, express the human transporters robustly in the liver, and show functional activity with some but not all statins.
humanized OATPs1B1 and OATP 1B3 mice have robust hepatic expression and functional activity in vitro and/or vivo with statins.
we have evaluated OATP1b1 and OATP 1b3 knockout mouse models and OATP humanized mouse models for the prediction of statin drug disposition and interactions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the Oatp1b knockout and the humanized Oatp1B1 and Oatp1 B3 mouse models for their use in predicting drug-drug interactions and drug disposition in humans.
the evaluation of humanized mouse models for the study of the pharmacokinetics and drug-drug interaction of organic anion transporting polypetide 1B1 (OATP1B)-dependent drugs.
the characterization and evaluation of OATP humanized mouse models as a translational tool for predicting drug disposition in humans.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the humanized mouse models of OATP transporters are promising tools for the study of the roles of these proteins in drug disposition, but further characterization is needed to define their utility for predicting drug disposition and drug interactions in humans.

the Oatp1/1b knockout mouse line is a valuable model for studying the role of OATP transporters in the disposition of drugs, whereas the humanized models may be useful to study the functional activity of the human OATP1Bs in vitro, but their utility for in vivo pharmacokinetic predictions in humans is currently limited.
OATP1A/1B knockout and OATPs1B1 and/or 1B3 humanization are useful tools for studying the role of OATPs in drug disposition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Oatp1/1b knockout model is useful to study the role of Oatps in the disposition of some substrates.

Oatp1 knockout mouse model is not suitable for predicting drug disposition and DDI in humans, and humanized mouse models of OATP 1B1/1B3 are not suitable for predicting the disposition of all statins, but they may be useful for some statins.
the humanized Oatp1B1 and Oatp1b3 mice are useful models to study the role of these transporters on the hepatic uptake of some substrates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
humanized OATPs may provide an opportunity to better understand the roles of OATPs in drug disposition and drug interactions in humans.
humanized OATPs may not necessarily recapitulate the full range of drug transport activities of the native human transporter.
these models are not yet ready to be used in a clinical setting.
